newsitem.title: USA: Calvin Grigsby rejoins minority-owned firm - official.
newsitem.headline: Calvin Grigsby rejoins minority-owned firm - official.

text.p: Calvin Grigsby, who resigned last month from Grigsby Brandford & Co. Inc. under the cloud of a federal probe, has notified Dade County, Fla., that he was rejoining his former investment banking firm.
"Calvin has told us that he is going to come back into the firm," county finance director Ed Marquez said during a meeting of the Dade County Finance and Trust Funds Committee. "He has unresigned."
Marquez said Grigsby relayed the information to him this morning by telephone.
People in Grigsby's office in San Francisco said the firm was now called Grigsby & Associates. No one at the firm was immediately available to comment on the change in name or on Grigsby's status.

The management shake-up at Grigsby Brandford, the nation's largest minority-owned investment banking firm, began on Sept. 17, when Calvin Grigsby, the firm's founder and long-time chairman, abruptly announced his resignation.
After he left, it was disclosed that authorities were investigating bond deals the firm handled in Dade County. Grigsby has not been charged with any wrongdoing in the probe.
In a recent statement, Grigsby's attorney said his client "strongly maintains his innocence."
Marquez said Grigsby told him on Monday that he resigned last month because he felt it was best for the firm, and that the firm could continue under the guidance of other top executives.

But earlier this month, newly-appointed Chairman Napoleon Brandford and President Suzanne Shank said they were also leaving. Both Brandford and Shank announced plans to join Muriel Siebert & Co. to open a new municipal bond unit for the company. About 40 employees at Grigsby Brandford are expected to join Muriel Siebert.

Despite the management turmoil, Marquez said Grigsby's firm remains senior manager on a proposed $168 million arena bond for Dade County, which includes Miami, if voters approve the issue in a Nov 5 ballot.
